about: Scam Guardian pattern dataset. Every check a message or link goes through is listed here, in the open. Each entry has a plain-language reason ('why') that is shown to the user when the pattern fires. Points add up: 0-14 = SAFE, 15-39 = CAUTION, 40+ = SCAM. Anyone can read, copy or improve this file.

patterns.label: Asks for your seed phrase
patterns.why: It asks for a seed phrase, recovery phrase or secret words. No real project, wallet or support team will ever ask for this. Whoever has the phrase owns the wallet and everything in it.

patterns.label: Send crypto first to 'verify' or unlock more
patterns.why: It asks you to send crypto first so a bigger amount can be 'verified', 'unlocked' or 'released'. Real airdrops and prizes never work like this. Money sent this way is gone.

patterns.label: Promises guaranteed or huge returns
patterns.why: It promises guaranteed profit or multiplies your money. No honest investment can promise this. Promised returns are the bait in almost every crypto scam.

patterns.label: Says you won an airdrop or prize you never entered
patterns.why: It says you won an airdrop, prize or reward. Winning messages that arrive from nowhere are the most common way scammers start the trap.

patterns.label: Pretends to be official support or the team
patterns.why: It claims to be official support, an admin or a team member reaching out to you. Real NEAR support never messages you first and never asks you to 'validate' a wallet.

patterns.label: Pressures you to act fast
patterns.why: It rushes you: act now, expires soon, last chance. Scammers rush you so you do not stop to check. A real opportunity can wait ten minutes while you verify it.

patterns.label: Tells you to DM someone to claim
patterns.why: It tells you to send a private message to claim or unlock something. Real projects use public pages, not private messages, for claims.

patterns.label: Hides the link destination behind a shortener
patterns.why: The link is shortened, so you cannot see where it really goes before clicking. Scammers hide fake pages behind short links.

patterns.label: Link imitates an official NEAR domain
patterns.why: The link looks like an official NEAR page but the real domain is different. Scammers copy the name and change the ending. Always read the part after the last dot: official pages end in near.org.
